supporting_observations.claim: At 13:48 UTC, FILE-SUN-01 launched the approved Arcvault agent as SUNRIDGE\svc-store, targeting the approved offsite backup endpoint.

The agent connected through the proxy to ingest.arcvault-backup.com, and the proxy recorded 640,000,000 client-to-server bytes; Zeek also recorded approximately 640 MB sent on the corresponding connection.
The network connection to the proxy is attributed by endpoint telemetry to the Arcvault agent process.

The alerted large transfer is consistent with the documented approved backup agent, destination, and expected several-hundred-MB upload size, so the available evidence supports a benign backup transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The logs attribute the connection to a process path and service account but do not establish the agent binary's integrity or signature.
The proxy and connection records show destination and byte counts, not the contents or business legitimacy of the transferred data.
The evidence does not establish whether a Nightly backup job was expected to run at this time.
claims_not_established: Whether the transferred data was the expected backup set.
Whether the Arcvault job was authorized to run at 13:48 UTC or was initiated on its normal schedule.
Whether the agent executable was unmodified.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: FILE-SUN-01 made an RPC connection to WS-ZADAMS-01; the supplied records show DNS resolution and TCP/135 activity but do not identify the initiating process or purpose. This is not evidence about the alerted backup transfer. (T260-00406, T260-00409, T260-00410, T260-00411)

Separate review: FILE-SUN-01 generated a failed network logon for disabled account svc_mgmt, followed by an RDP connection to DC-SUN-01 and an SSH connection to PROXY-SUN-01. These activities are outside the alerted transfer and should be investigated separately. (T260-00596, T260-00597, T260-00600, T260-00601)
